question: While observing a postpartum tubal ligation via minilaparotomy under spinal anaesthesia, you notice the patient suddenly complains of shoulder-tip pain and becomes bradycardic. Blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg. What is the MOST likely complication and required action?

answers.text: Vasovagal reaction from peritoneal handling; tilt the table head-down and administer IV fluids

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Vasovagal reactions do occur with peritoneal handling but should be considered only after excluding haemodynamic compromise from haemorrhage or pneumoperitoneum (in laparoscopic cases). The constellation of signs warrants immediate surgical assessment.

answers.text: Spinal anaesthesia spreading too high causing cardiac depression; administer atropine and ephedrine

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: High spinal is a recognised complication, but shoulder-tip pain specifically indicates diaphragmatic irritation — most likely from haemoperitoneum (blood tracking to the undersurface of the diaphragm) rather than high spinal alone.

answers.text: Intraperitoneal haemorrhage causing haemoperitoneum and diaphragmatic irritation; alert the surgeon immediately

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Shoulder-tip (referred) pain is the hallmark of diaphragmatic irritation from haemoperitoneum — blood tracking to the undersurface of the diaphragm. Hypotension and bradycardia further confirm haemodynamic compromise. This is a surgical emergency.

answers.text: Bladder injury from the minilaparotomy incision; insert a urinary catheter and observe urine colour

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Bladder injury is a recognised complication but does not cause shoulder-tip pain or the described haemodynamic changes. Shoulder-tip pain with hypotension points to haemoperitoneum.

overallFeedback.feedback: Shoulder-tip pain during abdominal surgery is referred pain from diaphragmatic irritation — most commonly caused by blood (haemoperitoneum) collecting beneath the diaphragm. Combined with hypotension, this is a surgical emergency.
Well done. Shoulder-tip pain plus hypotension during abdominal surgery = haemoperitoneum until proven otherwise. Diaphragmatic irritation from blood collecting beneath it refers pain to the shoulder.
